prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Provision for credit losses on loans at September 30, 2026 represents the amount of expense that, based on management’s judgment, is required to maintain the ACL for loans at an appropriate level under the CECL model. The determination of the amount of the ACL for loans is complex and involves a high degree of judgment and subjectivity. See the footnote titled “ Basis of Presentation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies ” in Bancorp’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 for detailed discussion regarding Bancorp’s ACL methodology by loan segment.

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expenses
nonint.text:
Total non-interest expenses increased $10.3 million, or 19%, and $25.6 million, or 16%, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods of 2025. Compensation and employee benefits comprised 59.9% and 61.3% of Bancorp’s total non-interest expenses, excluding one-time merger-related expenses, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026, compared to 62.6% and 62.2% for the same periods of 2025.

Total non-interest expense, excluding one-time merger-related expenses, attributed to the FM acquisition for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 totaled $5.7 million and $9.4 million. While the three month period represents the first full quarter of activity related to the FM acquisition, the nine month period includes just five months of such activity. One-time merger-related expenses totaled $678,000 and $3.0 million for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026. The vast majority of remaining one-time merger-related expenses are expected to be recorded during the fourth quarter of 2026.

Compensation, which includes salaries, incentives, bonuses and stock based compensation, increased $2.7 million, or 9%, and $9.6 million, or 12%, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026, as compared with the same periods of 2025.

Compensation and employee benefits comprised 59.9% and 61.3% of Bancorp’s total non-interest expenses, excluding one-time merger-related expenses, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026, compared to 62.6% and 62.2% for the same periods of 2025.

Total non-interest expense, excluding one-time merger-related expenses, attributed to the FM acquisition for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 totaled $5.7 million and $9.4 million. While the three month period represents the first full quarter of activity related to the FM acquisition, the nine month period includes just five months of such activity. One-time merger-related expenses totaled $678,000 and $3.0 million for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026. The vast majority of remaining one-time merger-related expenses are expected to be recorded during the fourth quarter of 2026.

Compensation, which includes salaries, incentives, bonuses and stock based compensation, increased $2.7 million, or 9%, and $9.6 million, or 12%, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026, as compared with the same periods of 2025.

tax.text: Capital and deposit based taxes, which consist primarily of capital-based local income taxes and franchise taxes, decreased $230,000, or 21%, and increased $186,000, or 7%, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods of 2025. Bancorp’s capital and deposit based tax expense is based on deposits held within various local taxing districts, as well as gross revenues generated within/appropriated to the state of Ohio, which is the only state Bancorp operates in with a capital-based deposit tax.

net.text: • Net income totaled a record $43.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, resulting in diluted EPS of $1.40, compared to net income of $36.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, which resulted in diluted EPS of $1.23.

da.text: Net occupancy and equipment expenses primarily include depreciation, rent, property taxes, utilities and maintenance. Costs of capital asset additions flow through the statement of income over the lives of the assets in the form of depreciation expense. Net occupancy expense increased $905,000, or 22%, and $1.8 million, or 15%, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026, as compared with the same periods of 2025, consistent with the impact of the FM acquisition and organic branch network expansion in addition to higher rent and depreciation expense. In addition to the six full-service locations added through the FM acquisition, four new branch locations were opened over the past 12 months, including Bancorp's first full-service location in the Bowling Green, Kentucky, which represents the first location opened in the new South Central Kentucky market. At September 30, 2026, Bancorp’s branch network consisted of 82 locations throughout the state of Kentucky, as well as the MSAs of Indianapolis, Indiana and Cincinnati, Ohio.

sbc.text: Compensation, which includes salaries, incentives, bonuses and stock based compensation, increased $2.7 million, or 9%, and $9.6 million, or 12%, for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2026, as compared with the same periods of 2025. The increase was attributed primarily to growth in full time equivalent employees, including the impact of the FM acquisition and annual merit-based salary increases. Net full time equivalent employees totaled 1,270 at September 30, 2026 compared to 1,140 at September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income - Overview
Net interest income.text: Bancorp’s primary revenue sources are net interest income and fee income from various financial services provided to customers. Net interest income is the difference between interest income earned on loans, investment securities and other interest earning assets less interest expense on deposit accounts and other interest bearing liabilities. Loan volume and interest rates earned on those loans are critical to overall profitability. Similarly, deposit volume is crucial to funding loans and rates paid on deposits directly impact profitability. New business volume is influenced by numerous economic factors including market interest rates, business spending, liquidity, consumer confidence and competitive conditions within the marketplace. The discussion that follows is based on FTE net interest income data.

intro.text: Stock Yards Bancorp, Inc. (“Bancorp” or “the Company”), is a FHC headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky and is engaged in the business of banking through its wholly owned subsidiary, Stock Yards Bank & Trust Company (“SYB” or “the Bank”). Bancorp, which was incorporated in 1988 in Kentucky, is registered with, and subject to supervision, regulation and examination by, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. As Bancorp has no significant operations of its own, its business and the business of SYB are essentially the same. The operations of SYB are fully reflected in the consolidated financial statements of Bancorp. Accordingly, references to “Bancorp” in this document may encompass both the holding company and the Bank. All significant inter-company transactions and accounts have been eliminated in consolidation.
